1001115.etyen:
A Nordic spelling variant of Alexandra, corresponding to the feminine counterpart of Aleksander.
The underlying name is Latin Alexandra (“female given name”), from Ancient Greek Ἀλεξάνδρα (Alexándra), the feminine form of Ἀλέξανδρος (Aléxandros, “male given name”). It is traditionally analysed as ἀλέξω (aléxō, “to ward off, defend”) and ἀνήρ (anḗr, “man”), genitive ἀνδρός (andrós), hence “defender of men” or “protector of men”.
In Norway, possibly first attested in 1817; the identification of the earliest bearer is uncertain.
Compare Danish Aleksandra, Swedish Aleksandra, Finnish Aleksandra an

1004443.etyen:
Unadapted borrowing from French sauvignon blanc (“Sauvignon blanc”), literally “white sauvignon”. The origin of French sauvignon is uncertain; it has variously been connected with other regional grape names and, tentatively, with sauvage (“wild”). The second element blanc (“white”) ultimately derives from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleyǵ- (“to shine”).
Compare the parallel borrowings Danish sauvignon blanc, German Sauvignon Blanc, Swedish sauvignon blanc and English Sauvignon blanc.

en.g: a female given name from Latin [in turn from Old High German, in turn from Proto-Germanic], equivalent to English Ottilie

1004699.etyen:
One of several Norwegian spellings of a female given name going back to Latin Otilia, originally Odilia, a Latinised form of Old High German Odila and Otila, pet forms of names such as Oda. The Old High German names are formed from the Germanic name element reflected in *audaz (“wealth, riches”), with a pet-name or diminutive ending. The spelling with th is historical and does not represent a separate /θ/ sound in Norwegian.
Compare Danish Othilia, Swedish Othilia, German Ottilie and English Ottilie (“female given name”).
